claims.text: Machine-learning interatomic potentials can determine melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can determine enthalpies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can determine entropies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can determine volume changes at melting in high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials improve the accuracy of thermodynamic-property determination relative to current methods.
Machine-learning-based methods improve computational or discovery efficiency relative to current alloy-design methods.
The proposed approach is applicable across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The proposed calculations cover high-temperature solid and liquid phases.
High-entropy alloys in the proposed workflow begin in a solid state.
Interatomic potentials are the structural mediator through which the intervention acts.
The proposed mechanism is ab initio molecular dynamics simulation.
Current methods for determining high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic properties are inaccurate or inefficient.
The performance of machine-learning interatomic potentials for high-entropy alloys is uncertain.
The approach should be validated by comparison with experiments and current methods using melting and liquid-state thermodynamic measurements.
Failure to improve both accuracy and efficiency relative to current methods would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention invokes machine-learning interatomic potentials, but the mechanism is labeled ab initio molecular dynamics. Ab initio molecular dynamics ordinarily obtains forces directly from electronic-structure calculations rather than from a machine-learning interatomic potential, and no hybrid relationship is explained.
